steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write a short introduction for our robotics paper on zero-shot Sim2Real transfer for map-free visual navigation using a BEV-based pretrained world model. Explain the Sim2Real gap, what existing transfer methods do and miss, and our setting with the CARLA simulator.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:

- Existing Sim2Real approaches and their shortcomings
- Need for a robust, low-footprint model
- Our setting: zero-shot Sim2Real visual navigation with CARLA data

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- RL mostly in simulators
  - real-world trial and error too costly
  - graphics/compute advances -> realistic simulators capturing robot info
  - domain gap synthetic vs real -> big performance drop when deployed: Sim2Real gap
- Existing approaches
  - train on simulation close to real data, or Domain Randomization (cite) / Domain Adaptation (cite)
  - train in sim, deploy to self-driving cars (cite); not trained in cluttered, pedestrian-rich environments -> don't generalize
  - Style Transfer for data generation with limited real data (cite, cite): promising but not learning optimal representations for navigation
  - end-to-end in simulator -> overfit to trained task, no generalizable representations (cite)
- Need: robust, low resource-footprint model for mobile robot in diverse scenarios
- Our setting
  - Zero-shot Sim2Real transfer for Visual Navigation without Maps, data from CARLA (Fig. 1)
  - Differential-drive robot in CARLA resembling real robot -> no control-pipeline gap, only perception transfer
  - large dataset of FPV + BEV image sequences from CARLA (cite)
  - trained only on simulated data, frozen, deployed on real mobile robot

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Reinforcement Learning (RL) has mostly been done in simulator environments, mainly because trial-and-error processes in the real world are prohibitively costly. Graphics and computational technologies have advanced, and so realistic simulators that capture the system (robot) information have developed significantly. However, there is a domain gap between synthetic and real data, and it causes a substantial performance drop when the models are deployed directly into real-world applications after training. This is commonly called the Sim2Real gap.

Traditionally, Sim2real transfer methods either optimize training on a simulation that is very similar to real-world data, or they use Domain Randomization or Domain Adaptation. Other works train on a simulated environment and deploy to self-driving cars. But these models were not trained in cluttered environments with many pedestrians, so they would not generalize to some real-world scenarios.
  - Style Transfer for data generation with limited real data (cite, cite): promising but not learning optimal representations for navigation
  - end-to-end in simulator -> overfit to trained task, no generalizable representations (cite)
- Need: robust, low resource-footprint model for mobile robot in diverse scenarios
- Our setting
  - Zero-shot Sim2Real transfer for Visual Navigation without Maps, data from CARLA (Fig. 1)
  - Differential-drive robot in CARLA resembling real robot -> no control-pipeline gap, only perception transfer
  - large dataset of FPV + BEV image sequences from CARLA (cite)
  - trained only on simulated data, frozen, deployed on real mobile robot

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Reinforcement Learning (RL) has mostly been done in simulator environments, mainly because trial-and-error processes in the real world are prohibitively costly. Graphics and computational technologies have advanced, and so realistic simulators that capture the system (robot) information have developed significantly. However, there is a domain gap between synthetic and real data, and it causes a substantial performance drop when the models are deployed directly into real-world applications after training. This is commonly called the Sim2Real gap.

Traditionally, Sim2real transfer methods either optimize training on a simulation that is very similar to real-world data, or they use Domain Randomization or Domain Adaptation. Other works train on a simulated environment and deploy to self-driving cars. But these models were not trained in cluttered environments with many pedestrians, so they would not generalize to some real-world scenarios. Some recent works, such as and, have shown promising results in dealing with the Sim2real gap by using Style Transfer for data generation with limited real-world data, but they do not focus on learning optimal representations for doing the navigation task. Also, models that are trained end-to-end in a simulator overfit to the trained task and do not learn generalizable representations. Because of all these practical considerations, we need to design a robust model with a low resource footprint that lets a mobile-robot function efficiently in diverse scenarios.

In this paper, we formulate a new setting for Zero-shot Sim2Real transfer for Visual Navigation without Maps, which uses data obtained from the CARLA simulator, as outlined in Fig. 1. We want to avoid any Sim2Real gap in the control pipeline and only focus on the perception transfer, so we built a Differential-drive based robot in the CARLA simulator that closely resembles our real-world robot. With this setup, we build a large dataset of First-person view (FPV) and Bird's eye view (BEV) image sequences from the CARLA simulator. The system is trained only on this simulated dataset, and then it is frozen and deployed on a real-world mobile robot.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Reinforcement Learning (RL) has predominantly been conducted in simulator environments, primarily due to the prohibitive cost of trial-and-error processes in the real world. With the advances in graphics and computational technologies, there has been significant development in realistic simulators that capture the system (robot) information. However, the domain gap between synthetic and real data introduces a substantial performance drop when the models are directly deployed into real-world applications after training, a phenomenon commonly referred to as the Sim2Real gap.

Traditionally, Sim2real transfer methods either optimize training on a simulation that closely resembles real-world data, or use Domain Randomization [1] or Domain Adaptation [2]. Other works [3] train on a simulated environment and deploy to self-driving cars. However, since these models were not trained in cluttered, pedestrian-rich environments, they would not generalize to some real-world scenarios. Some recent works, such as [4] and [5], have shown promising results in coping with the Sim2real gap by using Style Transfer for data generation with limited real-world data, but they do not focus on learning optimal representations for the navigation task. On the other hand, models trained end-to-end in a simulator overfit to the trained task without learning generalizable representations [6]. With all these practical considerations, it is imperative to design a robust, low resource-footprint model that enables a mobile-robot to function efficiently in diverse scenarios.

In this paper, we formulate a new setting for Zero-shot Sim2Real transfer for Visual Navigation without Maps, involving data obtained from the CARLA simulator, as outlined in Fig. 1. To avoid any Sim2Real gap within the control pipeline and focus only on the perception transfer, we built a Differential-drive based robot in the CARLA simulator that closely resembles our real-world robot. Using this setup, we build a large dataset of First-person view (FPV) and Bird's eye view (BEV) image sequences from the CARLA [7] simulator. The system is trained entirely on this simulated dataset, then frozen and deployed on a real-world mobile robot.

References:
[1] M. Tobin et al. “Domain Randomization for Transferring Deep Neural Networks from Simulation to the Real World” In 2017 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS) , 2017, pp. 23–30 DOI: 10.1109/IROS.2017.8202133
[2] Joanne Truong, Sonia Chernova and Dhruv Batra “Bi-Directional Domain Adaptation for Sim2Real Transfer of Embodied Navigation Agents” In IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 6.2 Institute of ElectricalElectronics Engineers (IEEE), 2021, pp. 2634–2641 DOI: 10.1109/lra.2021.3062303
[3] Alex Bewley et al. “Learning to Drive from Simulation without Real World Labels” In International Conference on Robotics and Automation, ICRA 2019, Montreal, QC, Canada, May 20-24, 2019 IEEE, 2019, pp. 4818–4824 DOI: 10.1109/ICRA.2019.8793668
[4] Gregory. Stein and Nicholas Roy “GeneSIS-Rt: Generating Synthetic Images for Training Secondary Real-World Tasks” In 2018 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation, ICRA 2018, Brisbane, Australia, May 21-25, 2018 IEEE, 2018, pp. 7151–7158 DOI: 10.1109/ICRA.2018.8462971
[5] Jingwei Zhang et al. “VR-Goggles for Robots: Real-to-Sim Domain Adaptation for Visual Control” In IEEE Robotics Autom. Lett. 4.2 , 2019, pp. 1148–1155 DOI: 10.1109/LRA.2019.2894216
[6] Alexander Amini et al. “Learning Robust Control Policies for End-to-End Autonomous Driving From Data-Driven Simulation” In IEEE Robotics Autom. Lett. 5.2 , 2020, pp. 1143–1150 DOI: 10.1109/LRA.2020.2966414
